variants.headline: Assembly votes the government out
variants.sub: The government has been voted out by the Colonial Assembly.
variants.body:
The Colonial Assembly has voted the government out. It is a decisive parliamentary event, though it does not by itself describe what follows. An assessment of {target} should start with the withdrawal of confidence and avoid announcing a successor that this report does not identify.

A lost confidence vote is a political fact with administrative significance. It does not supply an economic forecast. Firms should distinguish the institutional decision from assumptions about contracts, taxes or spending; those subjects require specific information, however tempting it is to interpret everything through the parliamentary result.

We take a sympathetic view of {target}. A parliamentary defeat is decisive for office, but it need not be treated as a final moral verdict on every person or position involved. Reliable assessment begins with particulars rather than a politically convenient assumption.

variants.headline: Confidence withdrawn
variants.sub: An Assembly vote has removed the government in {colony}.
